sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Sulh-i-kul**: Jahangir maintained his father's policy of **universal peace**, treating all religious communities with relative equality. 
• **Orthodox Reaction**: The Naqshbandi order, led by **Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi**, sought to reverse the liberal trends of the Akbar era, emphasizing the supremacy of Sharia. 
• **State-Ulema Nexus**: Jahangir balanced the influence of the **Ulema** (religious scholars) by maintaining a strong central authority, preventing them from dictating state policy. 
• **Key Metric**: The state's patronage of diverse religious institutions (temples, mosques, and Sufi shrines) remained a tool for political legitimacy.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Continuation of Akbar's practices; patronage to non-Muslim festivals.
Prelims: Often tested as 'continuity vs change'.
Reaction against syncretism; desire for Sharia-based governance.
Mains: Critical for analyzing the shift toward Aurangzeb's policies.

items.definition: The policy of 'absolute peace' or 'universal tolerance' that formed the bedrock of Mughal statecraft, ensuring stability in a multi-religious empire.
A Sufi order that became increasingly orthodox under Sheikh Ahmad Sirhindi, advocating for the purification of Islam from local syncretic influences.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Religious Patronage**: Jahangir continued land grants (Madad-i-maash) to religious figures regardless of faith. 
• **Judicial Autonomy**: The state maintained the Qazi system but reserved the right to override religious law in matters of state interest.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Balancing the demands of the orthodox Ulema with the necessity of Rajput and Persian support. 
• **Solutions**: Maintaining a 'middle path' through matrimonial alliances and administrative inclusion.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'J-O-S-H' (Jahangir, Orthodox, Sulh-i-kul, Harmony). 
• **Decoded Meaning**: Jahangir maintained 'Sulh-i-kul' (Harmony) despite 'Orthodox' pressures from the Naqshbandi order.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not assume Jahangir was as liberal as Akbar or as orthodox as Aurangzeb. He represents a 'transitional phase' where both tendencies co-existed.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Syncretic Statecraft' to describe the Mughal approach to religion in the early 17th century.

keyTakeaways: Jahangir largely upheld the secular framework established by Akbar.
The Naqshbandi order provided the ideological foundation for later orthodox shifts.
State policy was driven by political stability rather than purely religious dogma.
